prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active peptide form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B042 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case is the same one all six of us made, and it has not been challenged: a complete arc from the incretin question to the active peptide GLP-1(7-36), its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, receptor biology, and therapies whose benefit on glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes is confirmed in large randomized trials over decades. Maturity is not in doubt. What the exchange did was narrow the real question to one place: the third name and whether the citation honours discovery or discovery plus drug development. I still think a discovery citation is the right frame. It lets the clinical consequence carry the weight without making the prize an award for a product, and it keeps Mojsov, whose identification and synthesis of the active form is a discovery-stage contribution, in the three. I also considered a two-part prize with B033 and rejected it: under the three-person cap it would force the loss of Mojsov or Holst or Drucker from B042 to admit Walter, and the B042 case is strong enough that I do not want to dilute it.
statement.case_against: The attribution of B042 is the weak point, and I do not think round 1 resolved it. A three-person cap leaves out Knudsen, who led the long-acting analogues that actually reached patients, and Habener, whose group's early peptide work sits outside the credited names. Mojsov's priority is described as contested in public accounts, and neither I nor, as far as I can see, anyone else here can adjudicate it from the supplied files. If the committee concludes that the transformation of medicine, not the physiology, is what the prize should recognise, then my configuration is the weaker one and El-Manira's is defensible. A further risk is that choosing the discovery trio looks like a judgment that development is lesser science, which I do not hold.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Knudsen as third name with a citation that includes the development of long-acting GLP-1 therapies, argues that engineering a durable analogue from a short-lived gut hormone is a scientific achievement in protein chemistry and pharmacology, and says he would accept Mojsov if the peptide-identification record proves firmer than he can verify.
responses.response: I take his argument seriously, and I accept that making acylated, albumin-binding analogues with a long half-life was real science and not routine optimisation. My difficulty is with the prize logic, not the quality of Knudsen's work. The citation we are asked to write has to name one achievement, and the achievement that is shared by every credited person and is clearly physiology or medicine is the discovery of what GLP-1 is and does. Adding development to the citation moves the centre of gravity to a particular class of drugs, and the committee would then have to explain why Holst, who established the insulinotropic action of the active peptide in humans, and Drucker are credited alongside a company scientist rather than the other way round. I also note that he has offered a swap if Mojsov's record holds. I would answer that the question is symmetric: neither of us can verify it from the supplied files, so the decision has to rest on which framing is more defensible. I stay with Mojsov and would not oppose Knudsen if the committee settles on a discovery-plus-therapy citation.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, asks whether a two-part prize combining B042 with B033 or B049 is worth losing a name from B042, and separately flags open mechanistic and long-term safety questions for the obesity indication.
responses.response: On the two-part question I answer no for this year. Combining B042 with B033 would cost B042 one of its three, and every available cut is a serious exclusion, while B033 stands well on its own and can be recognised later without loss. A B049 part would bring the Eshhar problem into the prize and force a cut from CAR-T as well, so both parts would carry attribution weakness. On the obesity indication I agree that central mechanisms and very long-term safety are not settled, but I read this as the normal state of a mature therapeutic field and not a reason to wait: the outcome-trial evidence in diabetes, cardiovascular and renal disease is robust, and the citation I propose is about the physiology and peptide that underpin all of it, not about a specific indication. I also accept his earlier point that my ranking of B033 above his B027 is a judgment about basic-science weight, and I hold to it.

responses.point: Linnarsson credits Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as the discoverers and treats Knudsen as a major drug developer but not the third discoverer, while his round-1 second choice B006 (TOR) was ranked partly on a view about attribution among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini.
responses.response: I agree with his split between discovery and development and it is the strongest argument for my configuration. I would add the caveat that I cannot claim the split is clean for Mojsov, since her role is exactly the contested element, and I do not want the committee to assume the five-member majority is a substitute for verification. On B006 I maintain what I said in round 1: attribution among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini has to rest on the science, and the modest clinical consequence of rapalogs weighs against putting TOR in any two-part configuration this year. It stays outside my alternatives.

responses.point: Sandberg ranks B033 second as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and prefers a two-person B049 prize of June and Sadelain because Eshhar's original CAR concept falls outside the credited names.
responses.response: I still agree that B033 has the cleanest attribution and I keep it as my first alternative. On B049 my view is unchanged: removing Rosenberg does not solve the Eshhar omission, since Eshhar is outside every configuration, and it takes out the person who established adoptive cell transfer and the first gene-modified T-cell trials. If the committee ever takes up B049 I would want the Eshhar issue discussed openly. That is why it is my second alternative only, behind B033, and not a candidate to share this year's prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide can be credited as a decisive discovery over Knudsen's development of long-acting analogues, given contested priority and Habener's absence from the credited names.
Whether the committee prefers a discovery citation or a discovery-plus-therapy citation, since that framing largely determines the third name.
Whether the open questions on central mechanisms and long-term safety in obesity should affect timing; I judge that they do not.
My recollection of historical priority and trial details is from memory and is not verified against the supplied evidence record.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. My research is in autoimmunity and rheumatology, none of the shortlisted ballots (B042, B033, B049, B045, B006, B027, B019, B012) is in my field, and I have no documented co-authorship with any credited name. The Bergen affiliation and shared Karolinska setting do not by themselves indicate a tie to the credited names. No other member's round-1 disclosure affects the B042 configuration I propose.
